name: IsPrimitiveLabel.scaleRoots
summary: Take the root xi of c that is a primitive (q^r - 1)-th root of unity; a xi is a root of c.scaleRoots a, which is a label (scaling preserves labels) and irreducible (image under the multiplicative bijection scaleRootsEquiv(a)); its order equals that of xi because every prime p dividing ord(a) has p ord(a) | ord(a)^2 | M^2 | q - 1 | q^r - 1.

steps.claim: Let c be a primitive label of degree r: IsLabel(r, c) with c monic, squarefree, deg c = r and c(0) nonzero; c irreducible; xi a root of c in the algebraic closure that is a primitive root of unity of order q^r - 1, q = |k|. The four parts of IsPrimitiveLabel(r, c.scaleRoots a) are shown with the root a xi.
steps.lean:
IsPrimitiveLabel r c → IsPrimitiveLabel r (c.scaleRoots a) := fun ⟨L@⟨_, _, rfl, z⟩, I, ξ, w, h⟩ ↦
  ⟨L.scaleRoots a, I.map
  (scaleRootsEquiv a), _, scaleRoots_aeval_eq_zero w, h.eq_orderOf ▸ .iff_orderOf.2 ((Commute.all
  ..).orderOf_mul_eq_right_of_forall_prime_mul_dvd (h.isOfFinOrder (sub_ne_zero_of_lt
  (root_pow_card_pow_pred_eq_one I z w).2)) fun _ _ d ↦ by grw [d, ← sq, orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
  (by rw [← map_pow, ha, map_one]), hM, ← h.eq_orderOf, sub_one_dvd_pow_sub_one])⟩

steps.claim: c.scaleRoots a is a label of degree r.
c.scaleRoots a is irreducible: it is the image of the irreducible c under the multiplicative bijection scaleRootsEquiv(a) of k[X].
a xi is a root of c.scaleRoots a.

a xi is a primitive root of unity of order q^r - 1: it suffices that ord(a xi) = ord(xi) = q^r - 1; as a and xi commute, this holds if xi has finite order and p ord(a) divides ord(xi) for every prime p dividing ord(a).
steps.lean:
h.eq_orderOf ▸ .iff_orderOf.2 ((Commute.all
  ..).orderOf_mul_eq_right_of_forall_prime_mul_dvd (h.isOfFinOrder (sub_ne_zero_of_lt
  (root_pow_card_pow_pred_eq_one I z w).2)) fun _ _ d ↦ by grw [d, ← sq, orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
  (by rw [← map_pow, ha, map_one]), hM, ← h.eq_orderOf, sub_one_dvd_pow_sub_one])⟩

steps.claim: xi has finite order: it is a primitive root of unity of order q^r - 1, and q^r - 1 is nonzero since q^r >= 2.

For a prime p dividing ord(a): p ord(a) divides ord(a)^2, which divides M^2 because ord(a) | M (a^M = 1, also in the algebraic closure); M^2 divides q - 1 by hypothesis, and q - 1 divides q^r - 1 = ord(xi).
steps.lean:
fun _ _ d ↦ by grw [d, ← sq, orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
  (by rw [← map_pow, ha, map_one]), hM, ← h.eq_orderOf, sub_one_dvd_pow_sub_one])⟩
